sc-gov-2026-hakim-walid.name: Walid Hakim
sc-gov-2026-hakim-walid.bio: U.S. Marine Corps veteran who has worked in car sales, as a restaurant owner, police officer, political consultant and actor.

positions.stance: Proposes "South Carolina College Investment Grants" repaid through 10-20 years of service in the state, plus free school meals, childcare in schools and year-round schooling.
Supports a progressive tax system "where those who earn more contribute more," easing the burden on working and middle-class families.
Would reduce reliance on school resource officers and fund bullet-resistant classroom doors instead, aiming to end the school-to-prison pipeline.
Proposes a state-owned Carolina Insurance Company offering health coverage for $100 a month per individual with no deductibles or co-pays, plus auto and homeowners policies.
Would "limit property ownership to twelve residential properties per corporation or individual," excluding apartment complexes, to keep homes affordable.

sc-gov-2026-addison-michael.name: Michael Addison
sc-gov-2026-addison-michael.bio: Medical director, licensed asbestos inspector and property damage analyst, and community organizer with R.A.C.E.

positions.stance: Calls corruption "the single most important issue facing us today" and says nothing else will be solved until it is.
Proposes a surcharge on employers with 50+ employees that pay below a living wage, with revenue going to the Oregon Health Plan, SNAP and workforce training.
Supports a permanent moratorium on data centers, calling himself "the Only anti data center candidate."
Proposes expanding the Oregon Health Plan into a universal public option for every resident, with $0 premiums below median income and capped premiums above.
"Ports for Peace" would use the Governor's Port of Portland Commission appointments to set an ethical trade standard keeping ports out of active conflict zones.

nv-ltgov-2026-hansen-janine.name: Janine Hansen
nv-ltgov-2026-hansen-janine.bio: Longtime citizen lobbyist at the Nevada Legislature for Nevada Families/Eagle Forum and state chairman of the Independent American Party of Nevada.

positions.stance: Would use the office to "protect families, taxpayers and citizens and oppose the expansion and intrusion of state government into our lives."
Supports expanding tourism, especially outdoor recreation, to help rural counties and the state economy.
Advocates keeping Nevada's taxes low and says lowering them would increase economic growth and prosperity.
Says Nevadans must be vigilant in keeping communities safe "while protecting our fundamental Constitutional rights as citizens."

ar-gov-2026-shelby-colt.name: Colt Shelby
ar-gov-2026-shelby-colt.bio: Farmer and Franklin County landowner who worked on drilling rigs and later managed contracts for a Houston-based oil company.

positions.stance: Says too many Arkansans feel their government is hiding things and pledges to "restore open, honest government."
Would bring contract-management discipline to the state budget, saying "your tax dollars deserve accountability."
Opposes "school voucher schemes that siphon funding away from rural communities and local schools."
Opposes the proposed 3,000-bed prison in Franklin County as costly and poorly planned.
Says industrial data center expansion threatens to raise utility rates and pledges to "put ratepayers first — not corporate interests."

ar-ltgov-2026-kalagias-michael.name: Michael Kalagias
ar-ltgov-2026-kalagias-michael.bio: U.S. Navy veteran, former public school teacher and school security officer, and former volunteer firefighter.

positions.stance: Proposes cutting the state sales tax from 6.5% to 5%, removing local sales tax on food, diapers and hygiene products, and raising the standard deduction to $15,750.
Supports shrinking government and cutting spending, starting by ending the "mega-prison boondoggle."
Would ask the legislature to restore prior FOIA rules and would publicly post all actions taken by his office.
Says a child is created at conception and is "entitled the the same rights and protections as every other child."
Would work to repeal all laws infringing the right to keep and bear arms and recommend pardons for those convicted solely under them.

ne-gov-2026-lindstrom-brett.name: Brett Lindstrom
ne-gov-2026-lindstrom-brett.bio: Wealth management professional for nearly two decades and Nebraska state senator for District 18 from 2015 to 2023.

positions.stance: Supports "expanding pathways to success through education, workforce development, and entrepreneurship."
Calls for "predictable policy and reliable institutions," prioritizing "solutions over spectacle and results over rhetoric."
Says the state should be held in trust for those who come after, "Deciding for the next generation, not just the next election."

id-gov-2026-sand-paul.name: Paul Sand
id-gov-2026-sand-paul.bio: Former ten-year local city council member and Idaho property and business owner for 30 years.

positions.stance: Says his platform "is to permanently remove politics from state government and keep it out of local government."
Describes himself as "strongly opposed to abortion, open borders, and legalizing narcotic drugs."
"I strongly support substantial reductions in state agencies and state taxes."
"I am opposed to sending any money and weapons to any country."
"I am opposed to giving public benefits to any immigrant, legally here or otherwise."

id-gov-2026-stegner-john.name: John R. Stegner
id-gov-2026-stegner-john.bio: Former Latah County District Judge and former Idaho Supreme Court Justice.

positions.stance: Says Idaho has the highest grocery tax in the country and commits to policies that help families afford to live in the state.
Supports citizen-passed initiatives "including reinstating Medicaid access and Prop 1 should it be passed" and wants doctors to stay in Idaho.
Would work to undo the school choice voucher bill and return "the more than $50 million that was siphoned away from Idaho's public education."
Would support an Idaho statute requiring a warrant to protect residents' privacy from Flock camera data, citing mass surveillance concerns.
Says Idaho's public lands "are and should continue to be accessible to the public - full stop" and "are not for sale."
Would push to adopt approval voting in New Hampshire elections to address the third-party "spoiler problem."
Wants "cannabis to be fully legal" for adults.
Supports Defend the Guard legislation requiring Congress to declare war before the New Hampshire National Guard could be activated.
Would legalize medical psilocybin for PTSD, substance use disorder, and treatment-resistant clinical depression.

me-gov-2026-bennett-rick.name: Rick Bennett
me-gov-2026-bennett-rick.bio: Business leader and public servant from Oxford, Maine.

positions.stance: Would create a state-backed down payment guarantee so qualified first-time buyers can purchase a home with far less cash up front.
Plans to reduce pressure on property taxes and "eliminate corruption and make every tax dollar count" before asking families for more.
Would review and lower the authorized return on equity for investor-owned utilities to cut electricity delivery costs.
Pledges to pay providers "fairly and on time," cut administrative waste, reduce medical debt, and prioritize prevention and primary care.
Would unify Maine's birth-to-five system under single leadership with one integrated budget and invest in early childhood educators.

ri-gov-2026-block-kenneth.name: Kenneth Block
ri-gov-2026-block-kenneth.bio: Rhode Island businessman and data expert who founded a software company managing large-scale government systems.

positions.stance: Would pursue a regional New England health insurance marketplace, higher Medicare reimbursement, and "One Stay, One Bill" hospital billing; says he will not undermine the ACA.
Would direct Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative funds to bill relief for low-income households and push the 100% renewable goal from 2033 to 2040.
Supports removing income taxes on Social Security, barring credit-based auto insurance scores, and cutting taxes and fees on cell phone bills.
Would merge DOT with the Turnpike and Bridge Authority, merge DEM with CRMC, and assign a team to the Washington Bridge and failing IT systems.
His Cost of Living Relief Plan targets "hidden and regressive taxes, fees, and government-imposed costs" in everyday bills.

ri-gov-2026-gotra-jasjit.name: Jasjit S. Gotra
ri-gov-2026-gotra-jasjit.bio: Businessman who founded Alliance Security and SmartGreen Solar.

positions.stance: Would "run government like a business," publishing a state P&L and holding every agency to a budget with "no new taxes."
Pledges full commitment to teacher and firefighter pensions, saying "We fund it, protect it, and keep the word the state gave."
Would cut permitting delays and red tape and give small businesses "a direct seat at the table."
Would fully eliminate Rhode Island's tax on Social Security within the first two years.
Would bring AI tools into every classroom and retrain the workforce "for real 2030 jobs" to keep young people in the state.
Contrasts Rhode Island's $15.2 billion budget with New Hampshire's and Delaware's, saying Rhode Islanders "pay more than double for their government."
Proposes a permanent, unconditional "Pursuit of Happiness Dividend" paying Rhode Island residents $1,000 every month.
Says the return on AI, automation, robotics and data "belongs directly to the citizens," paid out as a data or automation dividend.
Supports a carbon and pollution fee on big polluters that funds an equal dividend to every citizen.
Questions beach, park, fishing and permit fees for using public commons and says the dividend would reclaim that public inheritance.

H6CA01285.name: James Gallagher
H6CA01285.bio: Assemblymember for California's Third Assembly District since 2014, former Assembly Minority Leader, former Sutter County supervisor, attorney and farmer.

positions.stance: "Make life more affordable for North State families through lower taxes, lower fees and fewer regulations."
"Enact tougher laws protect our communities, neighborhoods and homes from crime."
"Expand energy production to bring prices down."
"Defend our individual and property rights."
"Continue the tough border security implemented by the President."

H6CA01269.name: Mike McGuire
H6CA01269.bio: Former Leader of the California State Senate.

positions.stance: Says he will "fight to pass Medicare for All and keep rural hospitals open" in Congress.
Says billionaires and giant corporations rig the system and that he has made billionaires pay their fair share in California.
Pledges to hold ICE accountable, saying of the fight against the administration's actions, "I won't back down."
Cites leading the fight to double CalFire firefighters and bring billions in resources to protect the North State.
In Congress would "raise wages, take on corporate price gouging, and fight to bring down the cost of living."

H2CA06259.name: Jared Huffman
H2CA06259.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 2nd District since 2012 and ranking Democrat on the House Natural Resources Committee.

H6CA02309.name: Robin Littau
H6CA02309.bio: Enterprise Elementary School Board member, small business owner and U.S. Coast Guard veteran.

positions.stance: Calls to cut excessive regulation, support local control, and require responsible spending.
Calls to "End the Chaos & Find Solutions" and modernize citizenship requirements.
Supports a Parental Bill of Rights and "My Kid, My Call" with no mandates.
Calls to "Stop the Predators," adopt stronger deterrents, and support law enforcement.
Pledges to defend the Constitution and protect citizen rights.

H0CA03078.name: Ami Bera
H0CA03078.bio: Physician, former Sacramento County Chief Medical Officer and UC Davis clinical professor, first elected to Congress in 2012.

positions.stance: Believes national health, security and prosperity "require a transition in how we think about our relationship to energy use and natural ecosystems."
Says the health care system "consistently puts bureaucracies before the health of our patients" and an industry puts "profits before patients."
Supports an economy encouraging competition and innovation, job training especially in clean energy, and helping small businesses grow.
Believes "Medicare and Social Security are guaranteed promises and the key to a dignified retirement."
Says the U.S. must be "tough and smart" on securing borders, fighting terrorism, and the threat of nuclear proliferation.

H6CA03174.name: Robb Tucker
H6CA03174.bio: Nevada County Board of Supervisors member and former family business owner.

positions.stance: Would require federal agencies to consult counties early, create rural-impact reviews of major federal rules, and turn rigid grant programs into flexible block grants.
Wants federal dollars going to tools deputies use, like radios, vehicles and forensic equipment, and federal backing on border security and drug networks.
Calls his approach "compassion with standards," tying federal homelessness dollars to results like fewer encampments and more treatment beds.
Says to "manage the forest before it burns," letting counties, tribes and local partners clear hazardous fuels on federal land.
Supports more water storage, streamlined permitting for storage projects, and protecting local water rights from federal overreach.

H8CA01109.name: Mike Thompson
H8CA01109.bio: U.S. Representative since 1998, former California state senator, Vietnam veteran, and small vineyard owner.

positions.stance: Supports controlling debt and deficit through "a balanced approach that cuts spending, asks everyone to pay their fair share, and creates jobs."
As a hunter and gun owner supports Second Amendment rights and "commonsense policies like comprehensive criminal background checks."
Calls the Affordable Care Act "far from perfect" but "an important first step" toward health insurance for every American.
Supports helping "hard-working middle-class families navigate their mortgage hardships."
Supports comprehensive reform including a pathway to citizenship, college access for children of immigrants, and a guest worker program.

H6CA04222.name: Eric Jones
H6CA04222.bio: Business leader who helped build companies, focused on innovating healthcare models.

positions.stance: Takes no corporate PAC money, would fight to ban corporate PAC and special interest money, and would ban members of Congress from trading stocks.
Believes in congressional term limits and has "already taken a 12-year pledge."
Says "Politicians should never get to pick their own voters" and would restore California's independent redistricting commission.
Would close offshore "zero-tax loopholes," restore IRS enforcement and a fair corporate rate, using the money for working-family tax cuts.
Would bring federal regulators to bear on PG&E and author national standards making utility executives personally liable for deadly negligence.

H8CA04152.name: Tom McClintock
H8CA04152.bio: U.S. Representative and senior House Natural Resources Committee member; previously served 22 years in the California legislature.

positions.stance: Calls claims about human impact on climate change "dubious, political and unconvincing" and opposes policies that send energy prices soaring.
Believes "we need to restore our highway taxes for our highways" and modernize the highway system rather than fund mass transit.
Opposes attempts to restrict access to Yosemite and remove its amenities, and warns surrounding overgrown forests risk catastrophic wildfire.
Supports complete repeal of Obamacare, then tax parity for individual plans, interstate shopping, expanded HSAs and malpractice reform.
"Droughts are nature's fault; water shortages are our fault"; supports building more dams and overhauling environmental regulations blocking them.

H6CA05377.name: Michael Masuda
H6CA05377.bio: Engineer who worked at the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory.

positions.stance: Focuses on lowering housing, healthcare and energy costs, expanding rural housing access and reducing prescription drug prices.
Supports science-based thinning and prescribed fire, more federal land-agency staffing, home hardening incentives to lower insurance costs, and faster disaster aid.
Would protect Medicare and Medi-Cal, stabilize rural hospitals and clinics, expand telehealth, and reduce prescription drug and out-of-pocket costs.
Supports wildfire-resilience jobs, apprenticeships tied to local industries, rural broadband, and value-added agriculture.
Would expand federal programs financing affordable housing and streamline federal delays to lower building costs, especially in rural areas.
